Permanent housing replacement assistance may be necessary when the Housing

Division, after completing an inspection of a dwelling unit, determines that: 
a. Repairs are not feasible and that demolition is necessary to carry out the purposes of the CDBG Housing Rehabilitation Program.
b. Said dwelling unit is overcrowded, requires demolition, and that a larger dwelling is required to house the present occupants.
5.7 Owner-Occupants
It shall be the City's policy to financially assist the relocation of owner-occupants when it is necessary to replace those houses which will are economically infeasible to rehabilitate.
Assistance may include:
a. Housing replacement payment of up to $15,000.
b. CDBG loan and grant or Section 312 rehabilitation financing to fund the difference between the housing replacement payment and the total cost of replacement and rehabilitation.
c. Section 235 rehabilitation financing to fund the difference between the housing replacement payment and the total cost of replacement and rehabilitation.
d. Additional assistance may include: 
   Reimbursement for incidental expenses such as escrow costs, recording fees, closing costs, etc., for purchase of replacement dwelling.
2) Interest differential between old mortgage and new mortgage.
3) Moving costs as per relocation policies.
4. Temporary housing for a predetermined period of time until premanent replacement housing is available.
